In the evaluation of large language model negotiation capabilities, distinct styles and strategies were observed among the models.

One model adopted assertive strategies when proposing, leading to high utility gains, but showed a tendency to concede significantly when acting as a responder. Another model demonstrated balanced behavior, maintaining a consistent approach regardless of its role in the negotiation. A third model exhibited consistent behavior, frequently proposing resource divisions that were close to the theoretical fairness point.
